source.title: Enhancing Performance of a Deep Neural Network: A Comparative Analysis of Optimization Algorithms

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer results on training and validation accuracy using four small tabular datasets; this bears conceptually on optimizer-related generalization, but it does not reproduce the benchmark methods or settings in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and validation accuracies for seven optimizers on four datasets after 1000 epochs. It does not report a tuning search or quantify the generalization gap directly. Results for the optimizer comparisons are recorded below; cited prior-work claims are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD using training and held-out validation accuracy, extending V4's question to four small tabular classification datasets. It reports no learning-rate or schedule tuning procedure, so it cannot establish the comparison under V4's specified tuning protocol or challenge its image and language benchmark results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' stated preference: they declare Adam best across all four models, RMSprop second overall, and SGD and Adadelta unsatisfactory. This must remain attributed to the authors: their numerical results do not show Adam attaining the best validation accuracy throughout. Adam ties RMSprop on Toxicity, trails RMSprop, Nadam and Adamax on Masters, and trails Adagrad, Nadam and RMSprop on Titanic.
record.recipe_differences: A six-layer fully connected classifier is compared across seven optimizers on four small tabular datasets, using fixed batch size 8 and 1000 epochs; no optimizer tuning procedure is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the optimizer rankings and reported accuracies.
record.peer_reviewed: Advances in Distributed Computing and Artificial Intelligence Journal, Regular Issue, Vol. 9 N. 2 (2020)
record.problems: Small datasets (200, 400, 600 and 800 instances); no uncertainty estimates or stated repeated runs; validation split is called validation/testing inconsistently; hyperparameter tuning details are not reported; results include statements that several optimizers perform poorly despite their listed accuracies exceeding SGD on some datasets.
record.rows_left_out: None; all seven optimizer results on all four datasets are included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Image and language benchmarks; comparisons with momentum SGD; learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning; broader hyperparameter searches; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language models. The study does not isolate held-out differences at matched training performance.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that mitigate large-batch penalties; batch size is fixed at 8.
Dropout, weight decay and data-augmentation comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: V4 links represent a new-setting test of the optimizer comparison. These tabular results do not refute V4's scoped image and language findings or demonstrate the benefits of broader tuning. All adaptive endpoints either match or exceed SGD; none supports adaptive inferiority here. SGD accuracy remains almost unchanged throughout training, making optimization failure a material alternative explanation. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported, and the supplied text contains figure captions rather than readable plots.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image and language benchmarks; tuning breadth; weight decay; optimizer switching; word-level language models.

relationships.condition: Toxicity: Adam and RMSprop, 1000 epochs and batch size 8
relationships.reason: R2 and R5 reach 85% validation accuracy versus 80% for SGD in R1, limiting extension of adaptive inferiority to this tabular setting.
relationships.display_finding: Reported validation accuracy of 85% for Adam and RMSprop versus SGD's 80% remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Toxicity: Adagrad, Adadelta, Adamax and Nadam
relationships.reason: R3, R4, R6 and R7 match SGD's 80% validation accuracy in R1; no adaptive penalty appears in these reported endpoints.
relationships.display_finding: Reported validation accuracy matching SGD's 80% for Adagrad, Adadelta, Adamax, and Nadam remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Workshop: Adagrad and Adam, 1000 epochs and batch size 8
relationships.reason: R10 and R12 reach 83.33% and 88.33% validation accuracy versus SGD's 61.67% in R8.
relationships.display_finding: Reported validation accuracy advantages for Adagrad and Adam over SGD remain unverified.
